project: HM Land Registry public-estate OKF Bundle

requirements.statement: The public bundle shall contain discovery metadata, provenance, controls and links only, never property-level or bulk source data.
requirements.rationale: The discovery purpose does not require controlled or personal-level records.

requirements.statement: Every material record and proposition shall resolve to an authoritative publisher source, observation and derivation.
requirements.rationale: The bundle is a finding aid and must not become an unsupported authority.

requirements.statement: Completeness shall be stated only against a named, dated denominator with reconciled terminal outcomes.
requirements.rationale: No global page-level denominator exists across all associated source families.

requirements.statement: Publisher publication, modification, dataset release, coverage, observation, generation and release times shall remain distinct.
requirements.rationale: Catalogue modification does not establish data currency, validity or coverage.

requirements.statement: Every public record shall have an explicit access state, rights state and applicable rights-assessment reference.
requirements.rationale: HMLR source rights range from OGL to bespoke, paid, restricted, prohibited and unknown.

requirements.statement: The project shall not authenticate to, execute, search, copy from or monitor restricted HM Land Registry services.
requirements.rationale: Service terms and access models require accounts, licences, payment, keys or certificates and can prohibit automation.

requirements.statement: Credentials, certificates, tokens, signed URLs, personal-level records, user queries, forum posts and uploads shall not enter public artifacts.
requirements.rationale: Public accessibility does not remove privacy, security or ethical risk.

requirements.statement: Records shall retain source-native identity and use deterministic stable local identifiers; collisions shall fail the build.
requirements.rationale: Traversal-order or random collision handling breaks reproducibility and provenance.

requirements.statement: Documents, datasets, distributions, services, API products, repositories, versions and representations shall remain separately typed when materially distinct.
requirements.rationale: Collapsing source objects erases rights, cadence, access and evidential differences.

requirements.statement: Results shall present legal-reliance, official-copy, general/indicative-boundary, temporal-lag and coverage caveats when applicable.
requirements.rationale: Omitting a material caveat can turn correct discovery metadata into a harmful answer.

requirements.statement: The public site shall be a static GitHub Pages-compatible projection with no authentication, live restricted-service dependency or third-party tracking.
requirements.rationale: A static boundary is durable, auditable and consistent with metadata-only scope.

requirements.statement: Core discovery and source navigation shall work without JavaScript and target WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA requirements.
requirements.rationale: Progressive enhancement and standards-based HTML provide a resilient baseline.

requirements.statement: Search and rendering shall use bounded lazy metadata, not production data files or an eager whole-corpus first payload.
requirements.rationale: The source population exceeds a small-bundle shape and source distributions can be multi-gigabyte.

requirements.statement: Two clean builds from identical frozen inputs, code, policy and toolchain shall produce byte-identical governed output.
requirements.rationale: A release must be independently reconstructable without live-source drift.

requirements.statement: Every release question shall trace to a story, persona, source/evidence expectation, near miss and declared hard-failure policy.
requirements.rationale: Aggregate retrieval scores alone do not test safe task completion.

requirements.statement: A candidate shall have zero hard failures, MRR at least 0.80, Recall@10 at least 0.90 and source/caveat coverage of 1.00 on independently verified answerable questions.
requirements.rationale: Thresholds define a transparent first-release baseline while preserving categorical failures.

requirements.statement: Every governed input, generated artifact and validation receipt shall be covered by a closed checksum and provenance manifest.
requirements.rationale: Assurance evidence is meaningful only when it binds the exact candidate.

requirements.statement: Publication as an approved release requires owner approval of the exact version, digest, residual risks, claims and canonical Pages identity.
requirements.rationale: Successful generation or deployment is not release authorisation.

requirements.statement: Every declared public consumer shall be version-locked and executed against a tiny fixture and the exact release candidate; the canonical public deep link shall be exercised again after deployment.
requirements.rationale: Producer schemas and static file checks cannot prove that a real consumer can load, search, navigate and resolve the published artifact.

requirements.statement: A machine-readable artifact-dependency graph shall map governed inputs to generated outputs, consumer contracts and release gates; change-impact selection shall fail closed, and evidence may be carried forward only when every declared dependency root is unchanged.
requirements.rationale: Selective correction is safe only when affected artifacts and assurance evidence are derived from an explicit, validated transitive dependency model.
